title: Ten pull_request runs sit queued since Nov 11 on two old branches; find why they never started and cancel the dead ones
why: Coordinator 05:08 CST Nov 14 (REST total_count 10, all pull_request, created 2026-11-11 20:21 to 20:50Z; none started in about 2 days) and triage's own REST read at 05:08 CST (actions list_workflow_runs, status queued, total_count 10): checks runs 43095529627 (workflow checks 8314), 43097100885 (8315), 43097831985 (8316), 43098118148 (8317), 43098335788 (8318) and lane-touched-tests runs 43095529619 (2102), 43097100920 (2103), 43097831996 (2104), 43098118159 (2105), 43098335794 (2106). Two branches: glossary-records-half (head 0e41a456, one pair) and fix-check-after-main-merge (heads 408ea7a0, 517bad5a, cb576416, a4399310; four pairs). They look stuck or superseded, not a live wait. NOT read: whether those PRs are open or closed, why they never started (a runner label, a concurrency group, an expired queue), and what a stuck queued run costs. The coordinator did not decide whether to cancel; a cancel is a write on CI, so it needs a session that may do it and the owner's standing grant for the act (acts the cloud refuses: a cancel is not on that list). Check idea (unbuilt): a sweep that lists queued runs older than a set age whose PR is closed or whose head moved, and names them; any watcher states its cost first (process starts, files written, how often) and reads on demand inside a running process.
